provenance.version: n/a — not captured from a server
provenance.procedure: written by hand from the Torznab specification; see note
provenance.note: SYNTHESISED, and here is exactly what that costs. Every attribute in policy's vocabulary except size_bytes is unreachable from a capture this repository may hold: the only tracker safe to capture from in a public AGPL repo indexes Linux distributions, and a Linux ISO asserts no resolution, codec, audio or language. Both real captures in this corpus (torznab/jackett, torznab/prowlarr) therefore omit those attributes entirely — which is itself the fixture behind the `undetermined` path, and is real. This file is the opposite case and it is NOT real: the attribute SHAPES are taken from the Torznab specification, not observed on a server. It exists so that the extraction branches for resolution, video, audio and language are not branches nothing has ever driven. Treat a disagreement between this file and a real server as this file being wrong. It also carries three cases that are about extraction rather than transport, and those ARE modelled on measured behaviour: 'resolution' spelled both 1080p and 2160 (both spellings occur in the wild), an attribute present with an EMPTY value (measured — Prowlarr emits name="genre" value="" on every item, and it must count as absent, not as a determined empty string), and a value that cannot be read at all ('hd'), which must be left out rather than coerced to a number.
